title: Finite Q3 source-edge high-cutoff commutator stress
question: Does the source-edge graph commutator retain a cutoff-growing lower bound on explicit high-occupation Fock vectors when the target edge is fixed and the oscillator dimension is increased?
method: Hold the exact two-site Q3 target edge and source support {0,1} fixed while sweeping oscillator dimensions 3,4,5,6,8,10,12,16,20,24.
Construct the full and source-edge shifted weights and the right commutator operator C=[K_full,K_edge]K_full^(-1) for every dimension.

Evaluate C on the explicit high-core vectors |d-1,d-1> and |d-1,0>, compare each ratio with the global operator norm, and check the preregistered finite lower-bound slope (d-2)/4 on the diagonal vector.
Reconstruct the two-site matrices in a non-importing independent lane and cross-check dimension, vector-count, slope and scope fixtures in Lean R357.
finding: The primary lane passes 86/86 assertions and the independent lane passes 66/66. The integrated verifier passes 84/84 with Lean R357 PASS. Ten cutoff dimensions and twenty explicit high-core vector rows are covered. The primary maxima are graph=1.88843832098328, form=1.82494969105877 and global commutator=39.8709026914792. The diagonal high-core ratio grows from 0.292347675047599 at d=3 to 8.65366921692738 at d=24, giving a finite growth ratio of 29.60060898558; the lower bound (d-2)/4 holds on every listed row. Independent values agree within the 1e-7 lane tolerance.
decision_reason: The high-core calculation turns the earlier cutoff trend into an explicit finite-vector lower-bound diagnostic for the raw source-edge commutator coefficient. Since the coefficient grows while the graph and form constants stay near order one, this particular right-commutator input is not cutoff-stable and cannot be promoted as a uniform common-core history coefficient. The evidence remains finite and route-specific, so cancellation-aware and state-weighted topologies remain open.
boundary: T0 claim-nonbearing finite high-cutoff route stress on a fixed two-site graph. It is not an asymptotic divergence theorem, a global no-go, a common-core construction, a thermodynamic dynamics, an OS/KMS/GNS result, a mass-gap proof, a continuum result, C6, Sector A, Pre-A or Clay closure.

adversarial_review.check: The slope inequality is checked only on the manifest dimensions and explicit diagonal vectors; no asymptotic theorem is claimed.
The high vectors are finite-matrix basis vectors and no untruncated CCR is substituted.
The source-edge weight contains exactly the two onsite potentials and internal bond; crossing interactions are not included.
The commutator, graph and form constants are separately computed; form order is not used to imply commutator order.
The independent lane reconstructs the two-site oscillator Hamiltonian and high-core rows without importing the primary lane.
The finite growth rejects only the tested raw commutator coefficient as a candidate uniform input; cancellation-aware/state-weighted routes remain live.
Common core, cutoff removal, exhaustion, common alpha, OS/KMS/GNS, gap and continuum remain open.
R357 checks exact dimension/slope/count arithmetic and scope only; matrix norms remain Python evidence.

qft_interface.closed: A finite fixed-edge high-cutoff stress gives an explicit high-core commutator ratio and finite linear lower-bound diagnostic, independently reconstructed and Lean-bookkept.
qft_interface.open: An asymptotic theorem, a source/volume/cutoff-uniform common-core estimate, cutoff removal, direct D/delta-D Cauchy, exhaustion, common alpha, Hamiltonian-to-OS identification, KMS/GNS gap, continuum, C6, Sector A and Pre-A remain open.
qft_interface.tect_boundary: Auxiliary C6/Q3 route evidence only; no heat_root_incidence or canonical A1/R-192 production owner is supplied.

next_action: Replace the raw source-edge commutator coefficient with a cancellation-aware or state-weighted history estimate controlled on the common core, and require an analytic cutoff-uniform proof before common-alpha promotion.
no_overclaim: The finite high-cutoff growth is route-specific and does not establish divergence of the untruncated Q3 theory or rule out other dynamical topologies.
